review_notes: I read the whole file and the definitions it relies on in Basic.lean (isVar_iff_isHom, isHom_def, isHom_const'). I compared the simp setup with the sibling Sigma.lean and Subtype.lean, and searched the QuasiBorelSpaces directory for uses of the Quotient lemmas. I could not run Lean. Whether the @[simps] projection lemma competes with isVar_iff_isHom is inferred from how simps works on Prop-valued fields. I did not check the name or form of the generated lemma, and I make no claim that anything loops. Both findings are about unwanted expansion and an inconsistent attribute scheme, not about observed failures. The remaining declarations (isHom_mk, isHom_lift') have plausible simp/fun_prop tags, and I found no cycle.

findings.excerpt:
@[simp]
lemma isHom_def (φ : ℝ → Quotient S) : IsHom φ ↔ ∃ ψ : ℝ → A, IsHom ψ ∧ ∀r, φ r = ⟦ψ r⟧ := by
findings.problem: This is a global @[simp] unfolding lemma. It rewrites every `IsHom φ` for φ : ℝ → Quotient S into an existential over lifts. That is the definitional unfolding of the quotient structure, not a normal form. It fires on goals such as `IsHom (fun r ↦ ⟦f r⟧)` and turns them into an existential. The simp set then has to prove that existential, when `isHom_mk` composed with `isHom_comp'` via fun_prop would give a direct proof. The same file also applies `@[simps]` to the instance, which should produce a projection lemma rewriting `IsVar φ` straight to the same existential. `isVar_iff_isHom` is also @[simp] and rewrites `IsVar φ` to `IsHom φ`. So there are overlapping routes to one expression, and the file never says which is canonical. The sibling file Sigma.lean states its identical `isHom_def` (also `IsHom φ ↔ ∃ …` for φ : ℝ → Sigma) as `@[local simp]`. Quotient.lean is inconsistent with that. The unfolding lemma is used only by `simp only [isHom_def, …]` inside this file.
findings.proposed_change: Change `@[simp]` on `isHom_def` to `@[local simp]`, or drop the attribute and keep the existing explicit `simp only [isHom_def, …]` calls. That matches Sigma.isHom_def. Consider whether the bare `@[simps]` on the instance is needed. If it is kept, restrict it to the projections that are actually used, or add `-` simp exclusions where needed, so that only one rewrite direction for `IsVar` and `IsHom` on quotients remains.
findings.benefit: Downstream `simp` calls will no longer expand quotient homomorphism goals into existentials, so `fun_prop` and `isHom_mk` stay the way to prove them. Authors get one consistent attribute scheme across the Sigma and Quotient files, and the simp set has fewer overlapping `IsVar`/`IsHom` rewrites.

evidence.excerpt:
@[local simp]
lemma isHom_def (φ : ℝ → (i : I) × P i) : IsHom φ ↔ ∃ (ψ : Var I P), ∀r, φ r = ψ r := by

@[simp]
lemma isVar_iff_isHom {A : Type*} {_ : QuasiBorelSpace A} (f : ℝ → A) : IsVar f ↔ IsHom f := by

findings.problem: The attribute set is inconsistent. `isHom_lift` is tagged `@[simp]` but only `local fun_prop`. Its sibling `isHom_lift'` and `isHom_mk` have global `fun_prop`. `isHom_lift` therefore cannot be used by fun_prop outside this file, even though it is the natural rule for `IsHom (Quotient.lift f hf₂)`, a term with no argument-dependence, which `isHom_lift'` does not syntactically match. It is also a conditional simp lemma. Its hypothesis `hf₁ : IsHom f` has to be discharged by simp's own discharger, and it duplicates the role fun_prop plays. A grep of the repository finds no use of `isHom_lift` outside this declaration. So the simp tag buys nothing visible, and the fun_prop tag is hidden from downstream users.
findings.proposed_change: Decide the intended interface. If it is meant to be a general rule, use `@[fun_prop]` (global) and remove `simp`. If it is only a helper for `isHom_lift'`, drop `simp` and keep only `local fun_prop`. Alternatively, derive it as the `C = Unit`/constant-parameter special case of `isHom_lift'` so that only one lift rule is registered.
findings.benefit: Users of `Quotient.lift` get a predictable fun_prop rule, simp does not try to discharge `IsHom f` side goals for an unrelated lemma, and the simp-set stays small.
